rows.description: A child who once saw a classmate cheat decides everything about him is bad, including his drawing and his friendliness. One negative trait taints all.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager labelled as lazy or naughty by a teacher finds his good work ignored while every small slip is noticed. The label limits what others see.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student decides a group member is useless after one late submission and stops giving him tasks. The single flaw becomes the whole story.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A thoughtful lead notices when one error is colouring her view, and reviews the person's full record and context before deciding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child who is bumped decides the other kid is mean, not that the corridor was crowded. Others' behaviour is read as character while his own is excused by the situation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager assumes a friend who did not reply is uncaring, never thinking of a dead phone or a family crisis. Character explains everything, circumstances nothing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student calls a groupmate lazy without knowing he works nights at a job. Hidden pressures are invisible, so personal flaws seem the only cause.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A mature colleague asks what might be happening for the person before concluding he is careless, and stays open to both a situation and a habit being true.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child says he won because of his skill, but lost because of the referee or a bad bat. Success is owned and failure is outsourced.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager who scores high credits his brilliance and one who scores low blames the paper, the teacher or luck. Protecting self-image outweighs learning.
